title: Ops Spark Compact Battle Brief (alpha)
purpose: A compact, operationally-focused battle brief sellers can use live with prospects to accelerate pilots and reduce friction for Dedicated/Private conversions.
slides:
Slide 1 — One-line opener: Ops Spark Compact
- 90s trust kit + 2-minute pilot checklist for platform sellers
- Goal: convert exploratory pilots into committed reserved capacity by removing ops uncertainty

Slide 2 — When to use this brief
- Prospect is evaluating Redwood for production inference (hosted -> dedicated/private)
- Customer cares about latency predictability, cost per token, and fallback/resilience
- Use pre-demo, in-pilot troubleshooting, and renewal conversations

Slide 3 — Core seller pitch (short)
- ‘We give you predictable inference economics and a no-surprise ops plan’
- Quick evidence: curated benchmarks, pilot canary plan, automated fallback policies
- Close hook: 2-week safe pilot with explicit SLOs and rollback triggers

Slide 4 — Evidence cards (what to show fast)
- Latency heatmap: sample p95/p99 vs baseline (customer sample payload)
- Cost delta: token cost with intelligent batching/cache vs naive serving
- Recovery demo: simulated node loss -> automatic fallback to regional pool

Slide 5 — Pilot shape (recommended 10-day run)
- Day 0: onboarding + sample dataset + target endpoints
- Day 1-3: synthetic load + latency/cost baseline collection
- Day 4-7: canary traffic (1-5% production) w/ tracing hooks
- Day 8-10: scale decision + reserved capacity proposal

Slide 6 — Canaries & rollback heuristics (ops safe defaults)
- Canary SLOs: p95 latency < X ms, error rate < 0.5%
- Auto-fallback tiers: model-variant -> region -> lower-cost quantized variant
- Rollback triggers: 3 consecutive windows of degraded p95 or rising user-reported errors

Slide 7 — Quick technical checklist for SEs
- Confirm request shapes, max seq length distribution, and burst profile
- Confirm KV cache friendliness (prefix reuse) and embedding batch sizes
- Probe for network egress rules and KMS/HSM needs for Private

Slide 8 — Objections + short scripts
- ‘We built our own endpoints’ -> ‘Great. Most teams keep model dev in-house and use Redwood for predictable serving economics and fallbacks’
- ‘Latency too variable’ -> ‘We’ll run a 48h synthetic p95 test with your payload and show fixed routing policy’
- ‘Cost concerns’ -> ‘We’ll demo intelligent batching + autoscale profile and project monthly unit economics’

Slide 9 — Shared artifacts to drop in convo
- Mini SOW template for a first pilot (attached link)
- Pre-filled onboarding checklist for the prospect
- Example alerting playbook and canary metrics set

Slide 10 — Role cues (who does what)
- Seller: align success metrics and commercial ask
- SE: run the p95/p99 baseline, validate integration points
- Solutions engineer/CS: operational runbook + post-pilot migration plan

Slide 11 — Live demo script (3 minutes)
- Start: show console model catalog and perf profile for chosen model
- Step 1: run a single-request trace and surface token-level latency
- Step 2: kick off a tiny canary and show autoscale/fallback event in tracing
- Ask: get agreement to a 10-day pilot with defined SLOs

Slide 12 — Pricing & pilot economics (talk track)
- Emphasize predictability: provisional reserved capacity offer after pilot
- Show quick comparison: hosted on-demand baseline vs canary-optimized projected spend
- Mention add-ons: observability retention, compliance package

Slide 13 — Risk map & mitigation (for legal/ops questions)
- Data residency: VPC/private deployment option + KMS integration
- Auditability: request and token-level logs (retention options)
- Performance regressions: pre-defined rollback and canary window

Slide 14 — Post-pilot next steps checklist
- Deliverables: pilot report w/ latency/cost charts, recommended capacity profile, migration plan
- Commercial: pilot-to-reserved terms template, billing contacts, security signoff path
- Timebox: target decision meeting within 5 working days after pilot close

Slide 15 — Appendix: micro-eval snippets sellers can paste into SE runbook
- Lightweight curl to generate synthetic load + sample payload example
- Minimal tracing command and expected debug keys to request from engineering

Slide 16 — Notes to seller (talking tips)
- Keep conversations engineering-first: use metrics not marketing claims
- Surface known tradeoffs early: batch/cost vs p95 latency tradeoff is normal
- Offer to run the first synthetic test within 48 hrs — demonstrates speed and reduces friction
summary: Compact battle brief to help platform sellers rapidly demonstrate operational readiness and convert pilots into reserved capacity. Focuses on a 10-day pilot template, canary/rollback heuristics, quick evidence cards, objection scripts, and an appendix with technical snippets.
file_notes: Alpha version — intentionally compact. Wants feedback from 2 AE pilots before wider roll-out. Replace placeholders (X ms) with customer-specific targets during prep.
